clue.text: Dim … thick … astonishing! Nah, undo travesty of this …

definitions.text: Dim … thick … astonishing! Nah, undo travesty of this …

indicators.note: a travesty is a grotesque distortion, so the letters of the preceding words are distorted into a new order

explanation.surface: An exasperated outburst at an honour handed to someone the speaker thinks dim and thick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travesty of' shuffles all 26 letters of DIM, THICK, ASTONISHING, NAH and UNDO. The whole clue is also the setter's verdict on the honour, so it doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The former Conservative leader, architect of benefit reforms, was given a title in 2020, and the clue's sneer is aimed at exactly that honour.

clue.text: … fellow making people move pointlessly (and he was triumphant)

indicators.note: without a point: E (east, a compass point) is dropped from the word

parts.note: someone who turns tenants out of their homes is an evictor

explanation.surface: Continuing the theme: a man who forced people out of their homes, and who came out on top.
explanation.walkthrough: E is a compass point, so 'pointlessly' removes it from EVICTOR. The definition is a clause standing for the person it describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who was triumphant is the winner of a contest, a synonym-style description.

clue.text: With being kept on lates, fancy working independently?

indicators.note: the word for 'with' is held inside the rearranged letters
fancy as an adjective means elaborate or reworked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: and means together with

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether doing late shifts would let them work on their own terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lates' looks like late shifts, but it is just fodder with 'on' for the 'fancy' anagram, which then keeps the word for 'With'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stand-alone operates by itself, without needing any other system to function.

clue.text: Moving about

definitions.meaning: emotionally affecting, as a moving story is
concerning, as in a note ... on the matter

explanation.surface: Two words that seem to describe something in motion.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is emotionally affecting; the other is the preposition meaning concerning or regarding.

clue.text: Don't allow publication of government report

parts.note: to ban a book or report is to forbid its publication

explanation.surface: A call to suppress an official government report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report' looks like a document but is a loud noise, as of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is the sharp sound of an explosion or gunshot, the same as a loud noise.

clue.text: In town early just round the corner

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of the words town early

explanation.surface: Arriving in town early and close to one's destination.
explanation.definitionFit: Something just round the corner is close by, a synonym for being only a short distance off.

clue.text: Flying and deciding on route — no good leaving separately

indicators.note: the two letters depart from different places in the word, not as a pair

parts.note: plotting a course is navigation
N for no and G for good, standard abbreviations

explanation.surface: A pilot's flying and route planning, with the incompetent ones leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving separately' takes N and G out of NAVIGATION from two different spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying aircraft is the activity covered by the general term for operating planes.

clue.text: Woman close to return, a local admitted

indicators.note: the pieces are let in to the reversed word
the word for close is read backwards

parts.note: the close of something is its end
a local is a pub, abbreviated PH (public house)

explanation.surface: A woman nearing home who drops in at the pub on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is British for one's neighbourhood pub, abbreviated as on maps for public house.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, also borne by the nymph of Greek myth turned into a laurel.

clue.text: Transfer profitable part of hotel to which the writer's going

parts.note: H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet
the writer is the setter, I, and I'm going to need 'I have' contracted: I've
off means leaving or departing, as in 'I'm off'

explanation.surface: A company man disposing of a hotel chain's profitable division, where the writer is heading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the writer's' is read as 'the writer has', so I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: To hive off is to separate a section of a business and sell or transfer it as an independent unit.

clue.text: Head off crazy host

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word for crazy is cut off

parts.note: barmy is British slang for mad

explanation.surface: A deranged host of a party, told to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' removes the first letter of BARMY, British slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A host can mean a large crowd or multitude, like a body of soldiers.

clue.text: Time to stop 12? It's unacceptable

indicators.note: the time letter plugs a gap in the middle like a stopper

parts.note: twelve o'clock midday is noon

explanation.surface: Asking whether lunchtime is the moment to down tools, then calling it improper.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' looks like a reference to 12-across, but it is midday, NOON; 'to stop' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying a thing is not on is a British idiom declaring behaviour improper or unacceptable.

clue.text: Going round, say, a touch ironically, "He's made cuts but he is looking after you"

indicators.note: the word for one who cuts surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a carver is one who has cut meat or wood
EG, for example, is what 'say' means

indicators.note: just a touch of the word, its opening letter

explanation.surface: An ironic jibe at a minister who cut benefits while claiming to care for people.
explanation.walkthrough: The irony is the surface's jibe at a minister who cut welfare, while the cryptic reading needs only the first letter of 'ironically'.
explanation.definitionFit: A carer or caregiver is a person whose job is tending to someone dependent.

clue.text: Agreement to keep country short of money? It's not true

indicators.note: the word for agreement holds the other inside

parts.note: unity is harmony or agreement

indicators.note: lacking, so the money letter goes

parts.note: a realm is a kingdom

explanation.surface: A doubtful claim that consensus will keep a nation from going broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of money' looks like a broke country, but it trims the money letter from the word for country.
explanation.definitionFit: Unreality is the quality of being false or imaginary, something lacking any truth.

clue.text: Suffer — b----- man!

parts.note: the printed letter b, the other letters left as blanks
a man in chess is a piece, such as a rook

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry of 'Suffer, you bloody man!' with the swear word blanked out.
explanation.walkthrough: The dashes look like a censored expletive; only the B is used. A rook is a chess piece, and chessmen are 'men'.
explanation.definitionFit: To brook something is to tolerate or put up with it, usually in the negative.

clue.text: Government initiative causing trade boom? Sadly, that's wrong

indicators.note: the words trade boom go badly awry, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a cross, X, is the mark against a wrong answer

explanation.surface: A government policy blamed for a business boom, and declared misguided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' rearranges TRADE BOOM to BEDROOMTA. The bedroom tax was a 2013 UK cut in housing benefit for tenants with a spare room.
explanation.definitionFit: This UK welfare policy, the removal of the spare-room subsidy, was introduced under the coalition government.

clue.text: See 1
Henry not attending club function

indicators.note: the letter for Henry is absent, removed from the word

parts.note: a cosh is a heavy stick or bludgeon
H is the symbol for the henry, the SI unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A man named Henry missing a club social function.
explanation.walkthrough: 'function' looks like a party but is a trigonometric one: cos is cosine.
explanation.definitionFit: The cosine is a trigonometric function in mathematics, abbreviated in formulae.

clue.text: "Spirits raised, one's claiming Universal Credit from the start," country not concluding!

indicators.note: taking hold of, so the outer letters enclose the rest
in a down entry, raising reads the letters bottom to top

parts.note: one is I, and one's means one is

indicators.note: the opening letters of the two words
the final letter of the country is dropped

parts.note: Cuba is a Caribbean country

explanation.surface: Raised spirits as someone claims Universal Credit, the benefit, despite the country failing to finish anything.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'raised' reverses. Universal Credit is a UK welfare benefit, Iain Duncan Smith's flagship reform.
explanation.definitionFit: A succubus is a female demon in folklore, and these are such evil spirits.

clue.text: Alert — run aground

indicators.note: the letters are run around, set running into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An alarm call as a ship runs aground.
explanation.definitionFit: Being watchful and ready for danger is the idiom of staying vigilant.

clue.text: Free bar (and love) — genuine high-living?

indicators.note: the letters of bar are freed to move

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O
real means genuine

explanation.surface: An advert for an open bar and romance, promising the high life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' rearranges BAR to ARB. 'high-living' means living up in the trees, not luxury.
explanation.definitionFit: Tree-dwelling creatures live high above ground, the sense of living in trees.

clue.text: Investigators fail to be honest (somewhat twisted)

indicators.note: the word is given a slight twist, its letters partly rearranged

parts.note: to fib is to tell a small lie

explanation.surface: Federal agents accused of dishonesty and corruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat twisted' gives FIB a small twist: its last two letters swap, leaving F in place.
explanation.definitionFit: The US Federal Bureau of Investigation is the American federal police agency of detectives.

clue.text: Hospital in pleasant little corner

indicators.note: the hospital letter goes inside the word for pleasant

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: A hospital tucked away in an agreeable quiet spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a small recess in a wall, a nook or cosy spot.

clue.text: Favour one in party not of the highest intelligence

indicators.note: the pieces sit inside the word for party

parts.note: a bash is a party
a boon is a favour
I, the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Doing a favour for a not very bright guest at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Being apelike or oafish implies dim-witted, lacking in sharpness or brains.

clue.text: Essential to save energy

parts.note: bar means except, as does 'save' in 'all save one'
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Advice that conserving power is vital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save' looks like conserving, but it is 'except', which is BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Bare means basic or minimal, as in the bare necessities of living.

clue.text: One, and another in the way, getting flattened

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the second unit sits inside the abbreviation for the road

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road
another one, the word ONE itself

explanation.surface: Two people standing in the road and getting run over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flattened' suggests run over, but it is creases pressed out of clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes pressed with a hot iron are smoothed and made flat.

clue.text: 60% of teams ruled out by side one plays away

indicators.note: the letters are thrown out of order
three of the five letters, the first three

parts.note: R for right, one side

explanation.surface: Football talk: most teams excluded by a side that plays away from home.
explanation.walkthrough: '60% of' takes TEA from TEAMS; 'out' rearranges TEA and RULED to ADULTERE. 'plays away' is British slang for being unfaithful.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing away is an idiom for cheating on a spouse, which is what a faithless partner does.

clue.text: Appear to be heartless — prat!

indicators.note: the central letter, the heart, is removed

parts.note: to arise is to appear or emerge

explanation.surface: Calling someone a fool for seeming cold and unfeeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle I out of ARISE. 'prat' is British slang for the buttocks as well as a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are British slang for the backside, and both serve as insults for a fool.

clue.text: Hart is wild animal

indicators.note: the letters of hart run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A statement that a male deer is a wild animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The tahr is a wild goat-like mammal from the Himalayas, so an example of an animal.

clue.text: Wander aimlessly around Low Countries at first, then Hungary

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is used

parts.note: H is the international vehicle code for Hungary

explanation.surface: A tourist ambling about the Low Countries, then moving on to Hungary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low Countries' looks like the Netherlands and Belgium, but 'Low' is MOO.
explanation.definitionFit: To mooch around is British for loitering idly or drifting without purpose.

clue.text: See 1
Johnson takes a drink with nurse (hot stuff)

indicators.note: the name takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: Jo Johnson, the politician, gives JO
to lap is to drink as a cat does
EN, enrolled nurse

explanation.surface: A politician having a drink with a nurse, glamorously described.
explanation.walkthrough: Jo Johnson is a former UK minister, Boris Johnson's brother; EN is an enrolled nurse in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A jalapeño is a fiery Mexican chilli pepper, so something spicy to eat.
